_comment: The ONE declaration of the Panel's minimum WebView. Three consumers derive from macos_min/safari_min/webkitgtk_min/css_probes/js_probes and one guard covers all their edges: desktop/shell/tauri.conf.json (macOS install gate), interfaces/webchat/baseline-probe.js (runtime probe), scripts/check_webview_baseline.mjs (build gate). wasm_features is a separate declaration on this same file: the justfile's wasm-opt step reads it directly and fences the module's `wasm-opt --print-features` output against it, so there is no second copy to drift and it is not one of check_webview_baseline.mjs's edges. Never retype any of these values anywhere else. Rationale and the asymmetry of the guard's forward/reverse assertions: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-tauri-webview-resource-control-design.md sections 3.3 and 4.2.
wasm_features: Binaryen's own split of Bulk Memory Operations gating memory.copy/memory.fill specifically (src/wasm-features.h: 'Just the memory.copy and fill operations') -- same WASM proposal as --enable-bulk-memory, ships atomically with it, Safari 15+

Binaryen no-op kept only for CLI symmetry (src/wasm-features.h: 'this features is a no-op for compatibility... it does nothing. Binaryen always accepts LEB call-indirect encodings') -- not a runtime capability, no browser support required
